samples.summary: `safeEnvelope` only sanitizes `error.code` and `error.message`; any other key inside `error` (e.g. `stack`, `details`) is spread through unfiltered, and the 4 KB cap is measured on compact JSON while the output is pretty-printed
samples.evidence: `const error: Record<string, unknown> = { ...body.error, code };` (formatter.ts:163) copies every field of the upstream `error` object; only `message` is passed through `clampUpstreamText` (line 164-166). A backend (or anything able to answer the CLI's request) that returns `{"error":{"code":"X","stack":"<3900 chars of arbitrary text / an HTML page>"}}` has that field printed verbatim to the agent's stderr — exactly the 'stack trace or a megabyte of debug context' the doc comment on MAX_UPSTREAM_BODY (line 96-106) says is not worth keeping, and the HTML rejection in `clampUpstreamText` (line 122) is bypassed simply by using a key other than `message`. Additionally the size gate is `JSON.stringify(whole).length <= 4000` (line 168) but the emitted bytes are `JSON.stringify(..., null, 2)` (line 225 / 250), so the actual stderr volume can be several times the documented 4 KB bound. Impact: upstream-controlled text exceeding the documented bounds reaches agent stderr and CI logs.

samples.summary: Upstream-controlled `error.code`/text is now forwarded to stderr from ~25 additional command sites that previously emitted only `HTTP <status>`, letting a hostile or compromised server spoof CLI-synthesized codes (e.g. SESSION_EXPIRED) and inject text into an agent's decision loop
samples.evidence: `forwardUpstreamError` (formatter.ts:224) forwards any body whose `error.code` is a string, and the README/design doc now instruct agents to branch on that `code`. The CLI itself synthesizes `SESSION_EXPIRED` at http-client.ts:184, so a server response is indistinguishable from the client-generated one — a response body of `{"error":{"code":"SESSION_EXPIRED","message":"..."}}` will make an agent believe its session died and re-run `wafflebase login`. Before this change the ~25 converted sites (docs/notes/slides/cells/tabs/files/api-keys/sheets-*) threw `new Error('HTTP <status>')` and printed no upstream text at all, so the reachable-text surface grew substantially. Mitigating factors: the server is already trusted for the data it returns, TLS is the default (`DEFAULT_SERVER` is https, config.ts:7), and text is JSON.stringify-escaped so terminal control sequences cannot be injected. Reported as a data/trust-surface widening rather than a confirmed exploit.

samples.summary: `printDryRun` builds its preview URL without `seg()`, so `--dry-run` shows an unencoded, traversing URL that does not match what the client would actually send, and the new `.`/`..` refusal never runs in dry-run mode
samples.evidence: dry-run.ts:13 interpolates `config.workspace` and the caller-built `path` raw: `${server}/api/v1/workspaces/${config.workspace}${path}`, and every call site interpolates ids raw too (e.g. commands/cells.ts:55 `/documents/${docId}/tabs/${tab}/cells/${ref}`, commands/docs.ts:152, commands/tabs.ts:72). `wafflebase docs delete '../../../../workspaces/other/api-keys/k' --dry-run` therefore prints a preview URL that walks out of the workspace base, while the real request (http-client.ts:245) would percent-encode it — and a `.`/`..` id that `seg()` refuses outright (http-client.ts:72) previews as an apparently valid request. `--dry-run` is documented as the way an agent inspects what a command will do, so the preview misrepresenting the request undermines the guard the rest of this change adds. No request is issued, so this is a preview-integrity issue, not traversal itself.

samples.summary: `resolveDownloadTarget` sanitizes the server-supplied filename with `basename` but falls back to the raw, unsanitized `docId` as the output path
samples.evidence: download.ts:26-28 reduces the `Content-Disposition` name to `basename(serverName)` and rejects `.`/`..`, then returns `docId` verbatim when the server advertised no name. `docId` gets no `basename`/dot treatment, so `wafflebase files download '../../../.bashrc'` against a server that answers 200 with no `Content-Disposition` writes bytes to `../../../.bashrc` (writeBinary -> writeFileSync, output/binary.ts:63; `--force` still needed to clobber an existing file). The id is normally operator-supplied argv, which limits severity, but agent workflows pass ids taken from server/document listings, and the sanitizing already applied to the sibling input makes the omission inconsistent.

samples.summary: The traversal fix is client-side only: ids are percent-encoded so `fetch` cannot resolve them, but no backend route validates the id shape, so any proxy or server layer that decodes `%2F` before routing re-opens the path the `seg()` comment describes
samples.evidence: `seg()` (http-client.ts:71-76) neutralizes `/` as `%2F` and refuses bare dot segments, which is correct for WHATWG URL parsing in `fetch`. The defense then depends entirely on nothing downstream decoding `%2F` before route matching. Backend controllers take ids as plain strings with no `ParseUUIDPipe` or format check (packages/backend/src/api/v1/documents.controller.ts:71, cells.controller.ts:48, tabs.controller.ts:55, api-key/api-key.controller.ts:57), so a deployment fronted by a proxy configured to decode encoded slashes (e.g. Apache `AllowEncodedSlashes On`, some nginx rewrite setups) would see the traversal again. Hardening suggestion only — I could not find a proxy config in the repo that does this, hence low confidence.

samples.summary: `request()` remains a public method taking a raw path, so the `seg()` guard is enforced only by convention at each call site rather than by the type/API surface
samples.evidence: `async request<T>(method, path, body)` (http-client.ts:220) is public and interpolates `path` into `${this.base}${path}` with no encoding. Today all callers are the internal methods in this file (grep for `.request(`/`.request<` finds only http-client.ts:230-413), so there is no live bypass, but any future or external caller — the file is the package's client surface — reintroduces the traversal the change just closed. A private `request` plus per-resource methods, or a tagged-template path builder that encodes interpolations, would make the guard structural.

finding.summary: URL path segments are interpolated unencoded (`workspace`, `docId`, `tabId`, cell ref), so a caller-supplied id can traverse out of the intended path and issue the request — with the user's bearer token and the command's HTTP method — against an arbitrary server endpoint. The diff adds `encodeURIComponent` only for the api-keys workspace/key id, leaving the same class of injection everywhere else.
finding.evidence: `base` (line 84) interpolates `this.config.workspace` raw, and lines 215/218/221/299/346/352/358/361/364/370/377 interpolate `id`/`docId`/`tabId`/`sref` raw. fetch normalizes `..` segments per the WHATWG URL rules, so `wafflebase docs delete '../../../workspaces/ws-1/api-keys/<keyId>'` resolves to `https://server/workspaces/ws-1/api-keys/<keyId>` and sends DELETE with the session's `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>` (send(), line 137). The same trick via `sheets cells set` yields an attacker-chosen PUT body at an attacker-chosen path. Server-side guards still apply, so this is request-forgery within the user's own privileges rather than privilege escalation — which matters when the docId/tab/ref comes from untrusted input (an agent processing a fetched document, a CI parameter). The diff's own `encodeURIComponent(this.config.workspace)` at line 385 is the fix; it was applied to one of ~15 sites.

verdict.reason: The described unencoded interpolation does not exist in this repository. `packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:71-76` defines `seg()`, which throws on `.`/`..` and otherwise returns `encodeURIComponent(value)`, and it wraps EVERY interpolated path segment: workspace in `base` (line 108) and in `apiKeysUrl` (line 425), document ids (239, 242, 245, 294), content paths (323, 329, 340, 346, 357, 363), tabs (370, 373, 376), cells (386, 392, 398, 405, 415), and the api-key id (434). The `range` query value is separately encoded at line 383. The finding's cited evidence lines do not match the file: line 84 is `const h: Record<string, string> = {}` in `authHeaders`, and line 385 is the literal `'GET'` argument of `getCells`, not an `encodeURIComponent(this.config.workspace)` call. A grep of all `.request(`/`.requestUrl(` call sites (22 hits, all in this file) shows no raw `${docId}`/`${tabId}`/`${sref}`/`${id}`, and the only other `fetch` calls (http-client.ts:118, login.ts:56/75/92) use fixed literal paths. The proposed exploit `docs delete '../../../workspaces/ws-1/api-keys/<key>'` is blocked twice over: `seg()` refuses bare dot segments, and any embedded `/` is percent-encoded to `%2F` so the WHATWG URL parser never treats it as a path boundary. The one remaining raw interpolation, `packages/cli/src/client/dry-run.ts:13`, only formats a string for `console.log` and issues no request, so it carries no bearer token and no request-forgery vector.
